圓珠鼓屬膜鳴樂器，以繩連珠擊打鼓面發聲；中文文獻稱鞀、鼗，歷史可追溯至戰國時期，: The pellet drum is a membranophone sounded by beads tied on cords striking the head; in Chinese writings it is called tao or nao, and it goes back to the Warring States period, appearing in East Asia, South Asia, South America and elsewhere. Its development runs on two tracks: in Tibet, Mongolia, India, Thailand and Chinese ritual music it is used for religion or ceremony, while in East Asia small versions serve as children's toys or pedlars' rattles, and single, double and multiple drum forms appear.
圓珠鼓為膜鳴樂器，霍恩博斯特尔–薩克斯（Hornbostel–Sachs）編號2: The pellet drum is a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 212. The hourglass form, such as the damaru, is held by the waist and twisted back and forth so that two small beads on cords strike both heads. The East Asian stick form is held by a wooden handle or a vertical rod and, depending on size, spun along its axis with one hand, both hands or the palm, or swung side to side, so that the pellets strike the heads. A beginner first finds the heads, the beads and the cords, then twists or swings with a small, even motion so that the pellets strike in rhythm.
圓珠鼓的鼓身通常採用木質材料製作，多選用椴木、楓木等輕質硬木，以增強共鳴效果。鼓: The body of the pellet drum is usually wood, often light hardwoods such as basswood or maple, to strengthen the resonance. The head is animal skin, traditionally sheepskin or calfskin, treated to give the wanted tone. The beads are mostly carved from wood, some better products using hard solid wood or natural materials such as peach stones. The cords joining the body are cotton, hemp or nylon, for durability and flexibility. Modern versions may use light metals such as aluminium alloy for the rim or the reinforcements.
圓珠鼓音色輕盈而富有節奏感，帶有明亮而清脆的特質。當搖動時，圓珠撞擊鼓面產生的聲: The pellet drum's timbre is light and full of rhythm, with a bright, crisp quality. When it is swung, the sound of the beads striking the head is quick and lively, its range concentrated in the upper middle frequencies, without a definite pitch. Its way of resonating is distinctive: the two heads resonate together to produce rich overtones, which gives the tone a warm, soft foundation. Against drums struck with beaters, its sound is gentler and smoother, close to the soft effect of a shaker or a tambourine, yet it keeps the deep resonance of a drum. Its sustained sound makes a continuous, even stream, well suited to a relaxed and cheerful atmosphere.
圓珠鼓（Pellet drum）屬膜鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編: The pellet drum (Pellet drum) is a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 212. It is built as one double-headed drum, or as two hemispherical single-headed drums joined with the heads facing outwards and a pellet tied to each by a cord. When played, the handle is swung or turned so that the pellets strike the heads on either side. The pellet drum (Pellet drum) is a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 212. It is built as one double-headed drum, or as two hemispherical single-headed drums joined with the heads facing outward and a pellet tied to each by a cord. When played, the handle is swung or turned so that the pellets strike the heads on either side. Such instruments are found in Tibet, Mongolia, India, China, Korea, Japan, Thailand and Taiwan and are commonly used in religious ritual; small ones also serve as children's toys or street pedlars' rattles.
